texts.facts: With consent of the parties, hearing of the matter has been done through video conferencing and there is no complaint whatsoever regarding audio and visual quality. 2. The instant Interlocutory Application has been filed by one of the CNF agents dealing with Plain Gutkha products. 5. The instant writ petition, under Article 226 of the Constitution of India by way of pro bono public, has been filed seeking appropriate direction upon the respondents to implement the ban on sale of products like Gutkha, Pan Masala, flavoured/scented Tobacco, Kharra and similar products containing tobacco by whatsoever name called as per notification file no. 16/KHADYA (VIVIDH)/12-06/2017/98 (16) dated 05.07.2018 issued by Government of Jharkhand, Department of Health, Medical Education and Family Welfare with further direction upon the respondents for formation of a permanent policy banning the supply, sale and production of products Gutkha, Pan Masala, flavoured/scented Tobacco, Kharra and similar products. In pursuance to the aforesaid direction, 3rd Supplementary counter affidavit was filed by respondent no. 3- Principal Secretary (Health)-cum-Commissioner, Food Safety, Government of Jharkhand.
texts.arguments: 3. Learned counsel appearing for the applicant has submitted that, since in order dated 12.01.2021 passed by the respondents-State, there is no ban on plain Gutkha products as such the applicant does not want to press the instant Interlocutory Application. 7. Learned counsel appearing for the respondents-State of Jharkhand has argued out the case by placing the averments made in the 3rd supplementary counter affidavit, in particular order dated 12.01.2021 issued under the Signature of Principal Secretary-cum-Commissioner of Food Safety, Jharkhand, Annexure S to the 3rd Supplementary counter affidavit, wherein the State of Jharkhand taking into consideration various Rules and Regulations, the observations made by Hon'ble Apex Court as also the order passed by this Court in this 'Public Interest Litigation in particular order dated 16.10.2020 and 04.12.2020, at paragraph 20 of the order dated 12.01.2021 has taken following decisions: 20.In view of the above , there is imperative need to take strict action against sale of chewing Tobacco containing food additives and sale of twin packs of Pan Masala with adulterant Chewing Tobacco (chotu), in compliance with the notifications/orders of the State of Jharkhand and directions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court and High Court of Jharkhand and therefore ensure the following: (a).There is no sale of chewing tobacco products which is flavoured or scented or cloured by the use of food or food addictive such as spices, saffron kewda, menthol, lime, water, oil etc for one year from the date of issuance of the order. Fariyaad Foundation vs Government Of Jharkhand on 15 January, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176021041/ 3 (b).There is no of sale of twin packs of Pan Masala with adulterant Chewing Tobacco (chotu), though packaged separately but conjoint and sold from the same shop by the same vendor to circumvent Gutkha ban for one year from the date of issuance of the order. (c).There is no transport, storage, distribution and sale of Pan Masala and Tobacco Products without genuine e-way bills and invoices for one year from the date of issuance of the order. (d).There is no sale of tobacco products without authorization/license issued under the Jharkhand Municipal Corporation Act, 2011 for one year from the date of issuance of the order. Learned counsel appearing for the State further referring to Annexure A to the 3rd Supplementary Counter affidavit has submitted that in pursuance to the order dated 04.12.2020 passed by this Court in the instant 'Public Interest Litigation' for fixing accountability for search/seizure/raid effectively, the department has directed all the Deputy Commissioners of the State of Jharkhand to identify the entry points in each district and depute an officer who will be responsible for illegal entry of prohibited pan masala and tobacco. 8. Upon this, learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that although the government has made out the mechanism to effectively implement the policy decision pertaining to ban of the Gutkha etc. but the pertinent question would be how to implement it as this Court had also made reference in this regard in order dated 04.12.2020 to the effect that "strict vigilance at the entry point in each district of the State and accountability upon the officers who have been posted at entry point will not be fixed, the entire purpose of banning Gutkha/Nicotine will be frustrated", as such appropriate direction be passed since the same does not find mention in the 3rd supplementary counter affidavit. 9. Ms. Ritu Kumar, learned counsel for the intervener has placed the Intervention Petition, being I.A. No. 6024 of 2020, and has submitted that the effectiveness in implementing the ban order of State Government is of paramount consideration.
